title: Finite finitely presented algebras preserve w-contractibility
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and let R -> S be an algebra map. Assume S is finite as an R-module and finitely presented as an R-algebra. Suppose R is w-contractible: Spec R is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], its localizations at maximal ideals are strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and its connected-component space is extremally disconnected. Then S has all three properties, hence is w-contractible. No reducedness, flatness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For a prime ideal p of R, R/p has a unique maximal ideal: two maximal ideals would contract to distinct closed specializations of p in Spec R, contrary to w-locality. Let m be that unique maximal ideal contracted to R. The quotient R/p is a surjective image of the strictly henselian ring R_m, since every element outside m maps to a unit. The quotient theorem makes R/p henselian.

For a prime q of S, the domain S/q is integral over the henselian local domain R/(q intersect R). An integral domain integral over a henselian local ring is local (the already proved IsLocalRing.of_henselianLocalRing_of_isIntegral_of_isDomain in WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.IntegralLocal). Hence q has a unique maximal specialization. Since a prime of an integral algebra is maximal exactly when its contraction is maximal, the closed-point locus of Spec S is the inverse image of the closed-point locus of Spec R, and is closed. This proves w-locality of S.

For maximal q of S put m=q intersect R and A=R_m. The finite A-algebra B=A tensor_R S is a finite product of henselian local A-algebras D_i with finite residue extensions. Their residue fields are separably closed by Mathlib Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSepClosed, so every D_i is strictly henselian. The localization map B to S_q factors through one D_i: in the local ring S_q exactly one of the finite coordinate idempotents maps to 1. That factor map is local because it is compatible with A and its maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of A. Every fraction of B in S_q then comes from D_i, since its denominator coordinate maps to a unit and is therefore a unit in D_i. Thus D_i surjects onto S_q, which is strictly henselian by the quotient theorem. This proves w-strict-locality of S.

Apply the component-space theorem to the finite finitely presented R-algebra S and the w-strict-locality just proved. Its conclusion, together with w-strict-locality, is exactly the two fields of IsWContractibleRing S.
